tool.name: AreaAdjustedAccuracy

param.name: in_points
param.dialogReference: Reference points (feature layer) or a table with map and reference class fields.
param.pythonReference: Reference points (feature layer) or a table with map and reference class fields.

param.name: reference_field
param.dialogReference: Field holding the reference (ground truth) class code.
param.pythonReference: Field holding the reference (ground truth) class code.

param.name: map_field
param.displayname: Map Class Field (empty = read from raster)
param.dialogReference: Field holding the map class code. Leave empty to sample the raster at each point (point features only).
param.pythonReference: Field holding the map class code. Leave empty to sample the raster at each point (point features only).

param.dialogReference: Classified raster used to compute the mapped area of each class.
param.pythonReference: Classified raster used to compute the mapped area of each class.

param.pythonReference: Table with one row per class: sample size, mapped area, weight, user's and producer's accuracy with CI half-widths, estimated area and its CI, and overall accuracy.

param.pythonReference: Optional Markdown or HTML report with both error matrices and all estimates.

param.pythonReference: Confidence level for intervals in percent (95 gives +/- 1.96 SE).

param.pythonReference: Optional class names for the table and report.

param.name: out_matrix_table
param.dialogReference: Optional table of the error matrix in estimated area proportions (rows = map class, columns = reference class).
param.pythonReference: Optional table of the error matrix in estimated area proportions (rows = map class, columns = reference class).

param.name: users_interval
param.dialogReference: Interval for user's accuracy. Wald (default) is U +/- z SE, as in Olofsson et al. (2014). Wilson is the Wilson score interval: it stays inside 0-1 and does not collapse to zero width when every sample of a class agrees (U = 1) or disagrees (U = 0). Overall accuracy, producer's accuracy and areas always use Wald intervals.
param.pythonReference: Interval for user's accuracy. Wald (default) is U +/- z SE, as in Olofsson et al. (2014). Wilson is the Wilson score interval: it stays inside 0-1 and does not collapse to zero width when every sample of a class agrees (U = 1) or disagrees (U = 0). Overall accuracy, producer's accuracy and areas always use Wald intervals.

tool.summary: Estimates overall, user's and producer's accuracy and class areas with confidence intervals from a stratified random sample, using the stratified estimators of Olofsson et al. (2013, 2014). Mapped areas come from the classified raster (pixel count x cell area).
tool.usage:
Use the raster that defined the strata (the map the sample was drawn from).

Rows with an empty reference class are skipped and counted in a warning.

Leave the map class field empty to read the map class from the raster at each point.

The report is Markdown (.md) or HTML (.html) depending on the file extension.

When a class's user's accuracy is exactly 0 or 1, the report and messages give its Wilson interval, because the Wald interval has zero width there.

The estimators assume the sample was stratified by the classes of this raster (or is a simple random sample).
